projects.title: GovAssist
projects.description: A versioned public-policy assistant that applies deterministic checks, verifies its output, and returns cited evidence instead of unsupported answers.
projects.decision: We selected GovAssist because it gives each team member a clear technical responsibility and supports a complete source-to-answer demonstration.

projects.title: Lost and Found Portal
projects.description: A controlled lost-and-found workflow with structured reports, transparent match ranking, claim verification, notifications, and one recorded handover per item.
projects.decision: We did not select this proposal because similar campus reporting methods already exist and adoption would be difficult to prove.

projects.title: Placement Readiness Platform
projects.description: A placement-readiness system that maps skill evidence to versioned company criteria, identifies eligibility gaps, and builds focused roadmaps.
projects.decision: We did not select this proposal because access to reliable company criteria and placement data is uncertain.

projects.title: Semester Workload Balancer
projects.description: A workload-forecasting and constraint-aware planning tool that detects overloaded weeks and moves only work that can be completed earlier.
projects.decision: We did not select this proposal because the workload forecast depends on historical effort data that we would first need to collect.

planningPresentation.title: Planning Presentation v1
planningPresentation.changeSummary: Revised with the full development plan: a corpus-first build order, an LLM-aided drafting workflow with human-gated provenance, a multilingual voice layer, and a Postgres-based knowledge graph. Scope narrows to scheme eligibility only for the MVP; ITR and GST are deferred but the pipeline stays domain-generic.
planningPresentation.description: GovAssist is a grounded copilot: it answers government-paperwork questions with the exact rule clause cited, instead of a confident guess. English is the canonical internal language — translation happens only at the boundaries — so a citizen can read the UI, ask a question, and hear the answer spoken back in their own regional language, while every claim underneath still traces to a verbatim quote from an official document.
planningPresentation.scope: The MVP narrows to scheme eligibility only — ITR and GST are deferred, though the domain router, rule engine, and verifier are still built domain-generically so those agents drop in later without rework. Multilingual is a first-class requirement, not a nice-to-have: the app speaks regional languages through TTS and voice input, because the person most likely to miss a scheme they qualify for is the least likely to read a jargon-heavy English PDF. The very first build session targets only the corpus-building toolchain — local-only, no cloud, no database, no API keys — since the corpus is the long pole and the quality ceiling every later component depends on.
objectives: Answer with the exact clause cited, never an unsupported guess — a deterministic rule engine decides eligibility, the LLM only extracts and explains.
Every fact that can influence a verdict must trace to a verbatim character span in a committed source document; a span-validation gate enforces this in CI.
Ship voice-first multilingual access (Hindi, Punjabi, Tamil, English) as the accessibility feature, not a later add-on.
Keep translation off the critical reasoning path: verification runs in English against English clauses, then a round-trip translation check guards the localized answer before it's shown.
Never fail silently — a defined fallback ladder degrades voice, translation, and low-confidence answers with an honest message at every rung.
functions: Human-gated corpus pipeline: ingest → segment → LLM-assisted draft → span-validate → review → build (rules.json, graph.json, clauses.jsonl)
Deterministic rule engine over a restricted expression grammar (no eval()), returning ELIGIBLE / NOT_ELIGIBLE / INSUFFICIENT_INFO with the missing attributes
Verification agent that decomposes each answer into atomic claims and strips anything not backed by a rule fact or a retrieved clause
Multilingual core: Bhashini/ULCA-backed translate / speak / transcribe behind one swappable provider interface, with entity protection for amounts, dates, and scheme names
Knowledge graph compiled from the same rule packs (Postgres + recursive CTEs, no separate graph service) for reverse and cross-scheme queries vector search can't answer
Document extraction with user-confirmed fields, PII redaction before any text reaches an LLM or a log line, and no persistent storage of uploaded documents
intendedUsers: Citizens checking scheme eligibility, especially those more comfortable in a regional language than in English
A family member using voice in their own language to check eligibility on someone else's behalf
Administrators authoring and reviewing scheme rule packs through the human review gates
Future ITR / GST users once those domain agents ship — stubbed but not built in the MVP
externalInterfaces: Bhashini / ULCA — ASR, NMT, and TTS for the four supported languages
A free-tier LLM provider (Gemini or Groq) behind a swappable abstraction, used only to draft and explain, never to assert facts
Tesseract / PaddleOCR for document text extraction, with a manual-entry fallback
Official ministry guideline PDFs, committed to the repo with a checksum — never scraped, never fetched live at answer time

architecture.title: Web (Next.js)
architecture.description: Locale-segmented routes, the voice UI (mic button, playback queue, language switcher), and message catalogs for every supported language plus a pseudo-locale for overflow testing.

architecture.title: API — language and agents
architecture.description: FastAPI routers for chat, voice, documents, and schemes; the LanguageService facade (translate / speak / transcribe); the domain router, scheme agent, and verification agent.

architecture.title: Rules and graph
architecture.description: A deterministic rule engine over a restricted grammar, and a knowledge graph compiled from the same rule packs — one authored artifact, two projections, so they can never drift apart.

architecture.title: Corpus and scripts
architecture.description: One scheme.md per scheme: provenance, clauses, and rule conditions together, built through ingest / segment / draft / validate / build scripts with a human gate at every step.

qualityGoals.title: Performance
items: Time to first spoken audio under ~3 seconds
Deterministic rule evaluation stays off the network path
Translation and audio pre-baked and cached before any live demo

qualityGoals.title: Security & privacy
items: Uploaded documents processed in memory and deleted, never stored
PII regex-redacted before any text reaches an LLM provider or a log line
Extracted fields live in a session-scoped store with a hard TTL

qualityGoals.title: Reliability
items: A defined four-rung fallback ladder for voice, translation, and low-confidence answers — never a silent failure
Circuit breaker on the translation provider so an outage can't hang a request
Unsupported claims are stripped and, on repeat failure, replaced with an explicit ‘not confident’ response

qualityGoals.title: Maintainability
items: Every rule condition and graph edge carries a non-null source_clause_id, enforced in CI
Rule packs are append-only and versioned, with a diff script showing what changed between versions
One authored corpus artifact (scheme.md) compiles deterministically into rules, graph, and embeddings

risks.risk: The translation provider rate-limits or goes down mid-demo
risks.response: Provider abstraction plus a Web Speech API fallback, a circuit breaker, and pre-baked translation/audio caches run the night before.

risks.risk: Machine translation corrupts an amount, date, or scheme name
risks.response: Entity protection replaces those spans with sentinel tokens before translation and restores them after, with a round-trip test enforcing byte-identical preservation.

risks.risk: LLM-generated facts contaminate the knowledge base
risks.response: Non-null source_clause_id plus a verbatim span-validation gate and human review queue; a fabricated-triple fixture must be rejected in CI.

risks.risk: The knowledge graph and the rule engine drift into two different truths
risks.response: The graph is compiled from the same rule packs by build.py, never authored separately — a stale graph fails the build.

risks.risk: Scope creeps back to ITR/GST before scheme eligibility is solid
risks.response: Router, rule engine, and verifier stay domain-generic, but ITR/GST agents remain explicit stubs returning ‘not yet supported.’

milestones.title: Repo skeleton, provider abstractions, locale registry — SRS draft
Corpus toolchain + first hand-authored scheme.md; deterministic rule engine
Draft/validate/build pipeline; entity-protected translation — design doc
Graph traversal, verifier v1, TTS playback queue — mid-sem demo speaks all 4 languages
Full voice round-trip, round-trip translation check, translation QA pass
Document upload with PII redaction, multi-hop query set, metrics table
Deploy, pre-bake demo caches, polish and accessibility — final demo and report
